Filter state is deferred until the owner reference, identity lifecycle, cross-owner storage and legacy migration contracts are agreed and validated with consumers.

Find person retains identity without user details. Selection cancels pending and active lookups. Instances sharing a default or identical idValue still have duplicate input, hint and error IDs; the accessible name uses a translated phrase with an English fallback; pending names include an English translation-in-progress marker; real Welsh content and screen-reader acceptance are unverified. Multiple instances sharing one parent FormGroup still share a control and can issue duplicate lookups; replacing the parent group after initialization is unverified. Hint and error DOM IDs now include the supplied idValue, so external references require cutover verification. Consumer adoption requires application identity, accessibility and provider integration validation.

Task and work-type lookup default IDs can collide; task-name hint and error IDs are scoped when consumers provide distinct idValue values. Incompatible task-name cache data causes subsequent searches for that service to bypass cache without writing until picker recreation, increasing requests; recreation can encounter the same cache again. Real consumer dependency injection, Welsh error copy and assistive-technology acceptance remain unverified.
